description: Conformance vectors for the canonical N-Triples of a payload and for the request digest (ADR-A132 decision 4, ADR-A123). Verified by verify-vectors.py with openssl, which shares no code with a library.

ntriples.description: Three triples given out of order with one repeated. The lines are sorted and the repeat is dropped.
Only backslash, quote, line feed and carriage return are escaped. A tab, a non-ASCII character and an astral character are written as themselves, and a backslash before u stays two backslashes.
An xsd:string literal is written plain, other datatypes are kept, and a language tag is lower case.
The lines sort by their UTF-8 bytes, not by UTF-16 code units. U+FF5E (EF BD 9E) comes before U+10000 (F0 90 80 80), which UTF-16 order would reverse.

refusals.description: A blank node as a subject.
A blank node as an object.
An IRI with a closing angle bracket.

digests.description: Create. The payload part holds the new aggregate's triples. There is no expected seq, so that component is empty.
Replace under a patch log. Payload, add and del parts, in that order.
The triple C is in the add part and the del part is empty.
The same triple C is in the del part and the add part is empty. The digest differs from the vector before, since a triple's role is hashed.
Tombstone. The payload part is empty and still has its component.
Append of two events. One event part holds each row's type, pat:opSeq and pat:occurredAt triples with the event triples, which here include a node minted under event 1.
Append of a version under delta membership. Payload, then the added members and the dropped members in the add and del parts.
A target with a non-ASCII character. The length prefix counts bytes, so the target (18 characters) has prefix 19.
A triple that is in both the payload and the add part is hashed in both parts, not once.

payloadChecks.description: Every subject is the root or reached from it by owned edges.
A subject that no owned edge reaches is returned.
A node reached only by a reference edge is not the aggregate's to describe.
A comment reaches the aggregate through an inverse owned edge from its task.
The same comment on a task nothing reaches is outside, and so is nothing else in the payload.
A recursive owned edge reaches any depth.
A cycle in the data ends the walk.
hasSubtask is owned from a task and not from a milestone, so a node a milestone names by it is outside.
A payload that does not mention the root reaches nothing, so each of its subjects is outside.
With no owned edge the only subject is the root.
A family with no boundary shape bounds nothing, and the form of the payload is all that is checked.
A literal that looks like a query is an object and names no subject.

eventChecks.description: An event may name an aggregate as an object, and nodes minted under an event are its own.
An event triple whose subject is an existing aggregate would write into it.
A longer name that starts with an event's name, and a path that is not part/, are neither an event nor minted under one.
An append holds at least one event.
Each event of a batch has its own IRI.
opSeq is distinct within a batch.
A row has all four values. A row with an unbound one would make the VALUES row UNDEF, and a guard over it would read as true.

callerChecks.description: Every parameter present and of its kind.
A required parameter that is not given is named.
A parameter the operation does not declare is named, so a misspelling is not silent.
An epoch is exactly xsd:long on any store. An xsd:integer is refused where a store's own guard might pass it.
A plain string literal is not an xsd:long.
An xsd:long literal in canonical form passes.
A literal that keeps xsd:long and is not a number is refused.
9223372036854775808 is one past the largest xsd:long.
An IRI is not a literal.
A literal is not an IRI.
A digest is 64 lower-case hexadecimal characters.
The graph is the prefix, the root encoded as ENCODE_FOR_URI does, and the suffix.
The raw root in the graph name is not the encoded one.
An audit over no graph examines nothing, so the check refuses it.
A caller that allows it gets NothingExamined from the audit outcome and not a clean result.

auditOutcomes.description: An audit that returned a row failed.
No row, and the listed graphs held receipts to read.
No row and no graph listed is not a clean result.
No row and nothing to read in the listed graphs.
The key-claim and fork audits read fixed graphs and list none, so no row is clean.
A row means the audit read something, even over an empty registry.

referenceChecks.description: An object on a pinned edge is a version.
The identity of the organisation on a pinned edge is refused.
What the caller cannot say is a version is refused on a pinned edge.
A version on an edge by identity is refused.
An identity on an edge by identity passes.
Only the nodes the owned walk reaches have their edges read.

checkpointChecks.description: A checkpoint states pat:checkpoint true and lists all the members.
A list that leaves a member out is not full.
A list with a member the version does not have is not the list.
The list without pat:checkpoint true is not a checkpoint.
A version that is not a checkpoint lists no member and no mark.
A list the domain's property on a version that is not a checkpoint is refused.
